actions.name: Create fraudulent cryptocurrency investment applications
actions.description: Cyber criminals created fraudulent cryptocurrency investment apps to defraud cryptocurrency investors.

actions.name: Contact US investors fraudulently claiming to offer legitimate cryptocurrency investment services
actions.description: Cyber criminals contacted US investors, fraudulently claiming to offer legitimate cryptocurrency investment services.

actions.name: Convince investors to download fraudulent mobile apps
actions.description: Cyber criminals convinced investors to download fraudulent mobile apps used to defraud them of cryptocurrency.

actions.name: Use names, logos, and identifying information of legitimate US financial institutions
actions.description: Cyber criminals used the names, logos, and other identifying information of legitimate US financial institutions, including creating fake websites, to gain investors.

actions.name: Defraud at least 28 victims of approximately $3.7 million using a fraudulent app impersonating a US financial institution
actions.description: Between 22 December 2021 and 7 May 2022, unidentified cyber criminals defrauded at least 28 victims of approximately $3.7 million by convincing them to download an app using the name and logo of an actual US financial institution and deposit cryptocurrency into wallets associated with their accounts on the app.

actions.name: Send emails demanding tax payments before withdrawal
actions.description: When 13 of the 28 victims attempted to withdraw funds from the fraudulent app, they received emails stating they had to pay taxes on their investments before making withdrawals.

actions.name: Prevent victims from withdrawing funds after tax payment
actions.description: After paying the supposed tax, victims remained unable to withdraw funds from the fraudulent app.

actions.name: Defraud at least four victims of approximately $5.5 million using the YiBit app
actions.description: Between 4 October 2021 and 13 May 2022, cyber criminals operating under the company name YiBit defrauded at least four victims of approximately $5.5 million by convincing them to download the YiBit app and deposit cryptocurrency into wallets associated with their YiBit accounts.

actions.name: Send emails demanding tax payments before withdrawal to YiBit victims
actions.description: Following deposits, 17 victims received emails stating they had to pay taxes on their investments before withdrawing funds; all 4 YiBit victims could not withdraw funds through the app.

actions.name: Defraud two victims using the Supay app
actions.description: Between 1 November and 26 November 2021, cyber criminals operating under the company name Supayos, AKA Supay, defrauded two victims by instructing them to download the Supay app and make multiple cryptocurrency deposits into wallets associated with their Supay accounts.

actions.name: Enroll victim in a program requiring a minimum balance without consent
actions.description: In November 2021, the cyber criminals told one victim he was enrolled in a program requiring a minimum balance of $900,000 without his consent.

actions.name: Instruct victim to deposit requested funds or have assets frozen
actions.description: Upon trying to cancel the subscription, the victim was instructed to deposit the requested funds or have all assets frozen.
